correctness.rationale: The exact seven-state transition table is reconstructed from the published Wielandt coloring. A complete BFS over all 127 nonempty state subsets gives first singleton distance 31 and unique target state 2. Exact integer polynomial propagation on the shortest-path DAG gives \(z^6(1+z)^{20}\); an independent reverse-distance recursion reproduces the same coefficients. The packaged verifier replays these checks from the transition table and does not rely on a solver log.

value.rationale: The Wielandt family is a canonical slowly synchronizing benchmark whose extremal feature is minimum reset length. Counting all minimum reset words is the natural multiplicity companion to that threshold, and the exact binomial letter profile distinguishes a highly degenerate optimum from a unique-witness phenomenon. The seven-state instance is small enough to admit a complete transparent certificate yet large enough to have over one million optimum words, making the precise enumerator useful as a benchmark for shortest-reset-language algorithms.
